frame_note: frame_mm = square flange size: 42.3 = v1 motor_frame_mm (NEMA17), 57.0 = the NEMA23 listing above; corner chamfers are not modelled
purpose: MP5 joint load and reducer sizing review inputs. Every number is either read from a repository file by joint_loads.py (print settings, lengths, bodies, split parts) or listed here with its source or marked as an ASSUMPTION.
print_settings_note: read by joint_loads.py from models/fit-coupons-v1/slicer/*.bambu.3mf Metadata/project_settings.config (outer 0.42 + inner 0.45 wall, 15 % sparse infill, filament_density 1.26). ASSUMPTION: the model applies that wall thickness to every face (the profile has 1.0 mm top and 3-layer bottom shells) and is checked against one plate only.

NEMA17-40.source: 17HS4401 class seller listings (40 Ncm, about 280 g) - not a manufacturer data sheet; the ordered MKS motor is not measured

NEMA17-48.source: STEPPERONLINE 17HS19-2004S1 (59 Ncm, 48 mm) listing / manual; 390 g from a retailer listing - not checked again in this review

NEMA17-60.source: STEPPERONLINE 17HS24-2104S (65 Ncm, 60 mm, 2.1 A) listing; mass 0.50 kg is an ASSUMPTION (not found)

NEMA23-56.source: STEPPERONLINE 23HS22-2804S listings (1.26 Nm, 2.8 A, 57 x 57 x 56 mm, about 700 g) - not checked again in this review

driver_board_mass_kg.note: ASSUMPTION - MKS rear board + magnet + screws, not weighed

usable_torque_fraction.note: ASSUMPTION - share of holding torque usable at the working speed with margin for closed-loop stepper roll-off (24 V); to be replaced by the measured MKS torque/speed in the two-axis bench test

safety_factor.note: ASSUMPTION - printed reducer parts, unknown friction, stall margin

angular_accel_rad_s2.note: ASSUMPTION - about 115 deg/s^2 joint acceleration for the inertial term

payload_offset_from_flange_m.note: ASSUMPTION - payload + gripper centre 50 mm beyond the tool flange face (no gripper designed yet)

j6_payload_offset_from_axis_m.note: ASSUMPTION - payload centre 20 mm off the J6 roll axis (no gripper designed yet)

self_inertia_radius_m.note: ASSUMPTION (rough, NOT a bound) - every moving element also gets the inertia of a disc of the largest drum radius (104 / 2 mm) about its own centre; a long tube has a larger transverse inertia; motor rotor and reducer internals (reflected inertia) are not included

reducer_metal_mass_kg.note: ASSUMPTION - bearings, pins, shafts, inserts and screws of one joint reducer (6812 alone is about 0.05 kg class)

cycloid_printed.note: ASSUMPTION - printed cycloid with rolling pins; not measured

prestage_plus_cycloid.note: ASSUMPTION - cycloid 0.75 x belt or spur pre-stage 0.95 = 0.7125; neither measured

compound_planetary_printed.note: ASSUMPTION - split-ring compound planetary has higher sliding loss

gearhead_commercial.note: ASSUMPTION - typical value printed on low-cost NEMA17 planetary gearhead listings; not verified here

reducer_stacks_mm.note: every thickness is an ASSUMPTION for comparison - not a drawing, a product size or a minimum

candidate_drives.note: ratios are examples for comparison: 27:1 = Faze4 J2 and the Codex workbook example; the pre-stage ratios 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8 are ASSUMPTIONS (not designed)

faze4.note: J1/J4/J5 include belt stages, J6 is planetary; motor count and frame sizes are not in the local design-decision file

arctos_v2.note: J5/J6 are a differential wrist; MKS 57D appears on J1 in the sample configuration

sweep_26_1.note: the local purchase note lists a separate Sweep 26:1 cycloidal drive product and states it is not the whole Armold model; whether the Armold package uses the same reducer, and which NEMA17 lengths go on which joint, are open questions in that note

motor_rpm_at_usable_torque.note: ASSUMPTION - motor speed at which the usable torque fraction is assumed; joint speed = this / ratio
